summary: A 40-foot DNR tower north of Spokane, moved from Mica Peak; sources disagree on the 1955/56/76 dates; unused since 1994 and on private land behind a gate.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with a DNR flattop 14 x 14-foot cab and catwalk

access.note: Firelookout.com says the tower still sits on private property and visitors proceed at their own risk. Willhite says it lies behind the gate of the River Bluff Ranch community, with signs discouraging visitors from the last few hundred feet.

visit.drive_up: Road behind the gated River Bluff Ranch community; signs discourage visitors from the last few hundred feet

events.note: The first lookout on Mica Peak, a different site, was built in 1942 (per the Mica Peak page)
Replacement 40-foot DNR tower moved from Mica Peak to Lookout Point in 1955, per the Mica Peak page
Register: moved to its present site in 1956. Sources disagree with the 1955 move date.
Firelookout.com and Willhite: a nearly identical tower or lookout building was built here in 1956, preceding the present tower
A fire spotter planned to work on Lookout Point in June 1957, per a newspaper item quoted on a lookout-history site
Present tower built in 1976 (firelookout.com); Willhite says the current structure was moved to its present site that year
Staffed every season up to 1992, per firelookout.com and Willhite. The register says staffed until 1995.
Reopened during the 1994 fire season; unused since, per firelookout.com and Willhite
A housing development on the same hill opened up the drive to the lookout, per firelookout.com
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 18, 1999

corrections.why: Both the register and firelookout.com give a 40-foot tower. 40 feet is about 12.2 m.

corrections.proposed: 1976 for the present tower; an earlier tower or lookout building here dates to 1955 or 1956
corrections.why: Firelookout.com and Willhite both give 1976 for the present tower. The 1956 date belongs to the earlier building, and the register and the Mica Peak page disagree on whether the move was 1955 or 1956.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Mica Peak page says a replacement tower moved here in 1955. The register says moved in 1956. Firelookout.com says a nearly identical tower built 1956 preceded the present tower, which firelookout.com and Willhite date to 1976. Willhite says the current structure moved here in 1976. These are reported as a conflict and not settled.

Firelookout.com and Willhite say it was staffed up to 1992, reopened for 1994, and unused since. The register says staffed until 1995. The story gives the 1992 and 1994 dates from two sources and notes the register's 1995.
The register gives 3,094 ft (943 m), which matches the record's 943.1 m. Firelookout.com and Willhite both give 3,120 ft (about 951 m). Both figures are reported.

sources.title: Lookout Point Lookout - Spokane County Washington

notes_for_editor: Build and move dates conflict across four sources (1955, 1956, 1976), and the story says so. Staffing: the register says staffed until 1995; firelookout.com and Willhite say up to 1992 with a 1994 reopening, and the story reports both. Elevation: the register's 943 m matches the record; the other two sources give 3,120 ft. Access is private: firelookout.com says the tower sits on private property, and Willhite says it is behind the River Bluff Ranch gate. The story says not to climb it. Status standing comes from the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and is not restated elsewhere. The 1957 newspaper item names a private person; the story omits the name and the evidence quote covers only the spotter sentence. Read budget: six page reads (NHLR, firelookout.com, Mica Peak, Willhite, Weebly, FFLA list), plus an earlier grep of the FFLA list made during the batch of brief checks, so seven in all, one over the cap. The Weebly page was read by grep, so its body was only partly seen. Trailchick was not read. The record's 40.0 height problem is not here; the 12.0 m is a small rounding error against 40 feet.
